belief: “One more time won’t matter. I’ll quit tomorrow.”
belief_plain: One more time won’t matter. I’ll quit tomorrow
origins: “One more time won’t matter. I’ll quit tomorrow” is a kind sentence people tell themselves so today does not have to change. Tomorrow stays clean because it never arrives. This is not proof that you are a liar or a hopeless case. It is a very common way to lower the fear of stopping. The mercy in it, if you can hear it, is that you already know you want a different day. The lie is that today is too small to matter and that a promise about tomorrow is the same thing as a plan. A plan includes a person who can help, and a doctor if stopping could make you sick. If you want help, call the SAMHSA National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357. Do not try to stop or withdraw on your own if that could make you sick. A doctor can help you do it safely, and a counselor can walk with you. Needing that help is not a failure.
self: I have said it before, so saying it again is pointless.
Today is already ruined, so I might as well.
If I ask for help today, I have admitted I cannot quit on my own schedule.
God is keeping score of every delay.
replacement: One more time does matter, and tomorrow is not a plan. I can take one honest step today, with help.
